metadata.name: env
metadata.displayName: env - Run a program in a modified environment
metadata.description: Run a program in a modified environment

installation.note: env is a built-in command available on all Linux systems by default

overview.summary: The env command runs programs in a modified environment. It can set, modify, or clear environment variables for the execution of a command. It's also commonly used to find and execute programs in the PATH, and is often used in shebang lines of scripts to ensure portability.
when_to_use: Run commands with modified environment variables
Use in script shebangs for portability

syntax.description: Without a command, env prints the current environment. With NAME=VALUE pairs, it sets those variables. With a command, it runs the command with the modified environment.

options.use_case: Run command with completely clean environment

misconceptions.title: Permanent changes
misconceptions.reality: env only modifies environment for the specific command execution. Changes don't persist after the command finishes.
misconceptions.tip: env changes are temporary and only affect the executed command

misconceptions.title: Same as export
misconceptions.misconception: env and export do the same thing
misconceptions.reality: export sets variables in current shell session, env sets them only for a single command execution
misconceptions.tip: Use export for shell session, env for single command

common_pitfalls.description: Using -i creates empty environment, so commands won't be found
common_pitfalls.solution: Always specify PATH when using -i: 'env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin command'
Use NAME=value format with no spaces around equals sign

common_pitfalls.description: Some systems have limitations on shebang line length
common_pitfalls.solution: Keep shebang lines short, or use -S option for complex cases

related_commands.description: export sets environment variables in current shell, env sets them for single command
printenv displays environment variables, similar to 'env' without arguments
set shows shell variables, env shows environment variables
unset removes variables in current shell, env -u removes for single command

best_practices: Use env in shebang lines for portability: '#!/usr/bin/env python3'
Always specify PATH when using -i (ignore-environment) option
Use env to test programs with different environments
Combine with other commands for clean execution contexts
Use -v for debugging environment variable issues
performance_tips: env has minimal overhead - it's very fast
Using -i with minimal PATH can speed up command lookup
env is often faster than modifying environment in shell and then running command

additional_notes.shebang_usage: env is commonly used in shebang lines (#!/usr/bin/env) to find interpreters in PATH
additional_notes.portability: Using env in shebangs makes scripts more portable across different systems
additional_notes.clean_execution: env -i provides clean execution environment for testing and security
